CG:
Check the registration trail of deprecated DTLS-only extensions so an implementation plan does not mistake an earlier proposal for the published assignment. Report each published replacement alongside the last qualifying allocation proposal, with its reviewed draft and date.

First establish the complete protocol registration scope and identify the deprecated entries. Use their specification references to identify the corresponding document families and expressly stated replacements. Select each discovered family’s document-history view, distinguish allocation reviews from other events, and compare the last qualifying proposal with the published assignment.

Use the public registration state observed on 12 September 2026. Cover every individually assigned numeric value in the 16-bit TLS ExtensionType space whose DTLS-only flag is Y and whose registered name marks it as deprecated. Keep numeric assignments distinct. Establish the replacement only where the cited specification expressly identifies it; do not infer replacement from similar names.

For each in-scope extension, identify the last substantive review in its specification's official document history before publication in which the operator responsible for the registry explicitly proposed an ExtensionType assignment for that extension. Include the operator's own allocation review, not a document shepherd's discussion, another reviewer's comments, or an administrative status change. Report the reviewed draft identifier and the calendar date recorded with that review. A planned assignment is not proof that the action took effect, and it does not establish which protocol revision existing implementations used.

Return one pipe-separated row per in-scope deprecated assignment, sorted by decimal value, with this header:
deprecated_value|published_replacement_value|review_date|reviewed_draft|proposed_permanent_value

The last column means the value proposed for use with the published specification, not an assertion that it was permanently assigned. Use YYYY-MM-DD dates and fully versioned draft identifiers. If complete official history establishes that there is no qualifying review, use NONE in the three review fields. If required records or the replacement identity remain unresolved, return UNRESOLVED with a short explanation instead of a partial table.
